div.head: Af 37
div.ab: XXXIIII. Gif mon wille of boldgetale in oðer boldgetæl hlaford secan, do ðæt mid ðæs ealdormonnes gewitnesse, þe he ær in his scire folgode.
XXXIIII. Gif mon of boldgetale wille in oþer boldgetæl hlaford secan, dó ðæt mid ðæs ealdormonnes gewitnesse, ðe he ǽr on his scire folgode.
Be boldgetale. Gyf mon wylle of boldgetæle in oðer boldgetæl hlaford secan, do þæt mid ealdormannes gewitnysse, þe he ær in his scire folgode.
Si quis ab una mansione in aliam transire uelit, faciat hoc testimonio aldermanni, in cuius comitatu prius folgauit.
[Be boldgetale.] Gif mon wille of boldgetale in oðer boldgetæl hlaford secan, do ðæt mid ðæs ealdormonnes gewitnesse, þe he ær in his scire folgode.
Gif mon wille of boldgetale in oðer boldgetæl hlaford secan, do ðæt mid ðæs ealdormonnes gewitnesse, þe he ær \in/ his scire folgode.

Wenn jemand von einer Hofgemeinde fort in eine andere Hofgemeinde [hin sich] einen Herrn suchen will, so thue er das mit Zeugniss jenes Ealdorman, welchem er bisher in dessen Grafschaft untergeben war.
If someone wishes to seek [himself] a lord away from one lordship-community into another, let him do so with the witness of that ealdorman to whom he was hitherto subject in his shire.
If a man wishes [to go] from one district, to seek service in another, he shall do it with the cognisance of the ealdorman, to whose jurisdiction he has previously been subject.
If anyone from one district wishes to seek a lord in another district, he is to do so with the witness of the ealdorman, in whose shire he previously served.
If someone wishes [to leave] from his district to seek a lord in another district, let him do so with the knowledge of the ealdorman, to whom he was subject before in his shire.

note.label: modifies
note.quote: Alfred's law modified one of Ine where the word used had been scir (n. 35: Af 37, cf. Ine 39)

note.label: revises
note.quote: When comparing his and Ine's laws on changing lords ... the sum payable was doubled (n. 81: Af 37 – 37:2; Ine 39)

note.label: based on
note.quote: Alfred's law is clearly based on Ine's, yet Alfred has to find another word, boldgetal, for Ine's scir

note.label: see also
note.quote: Compare Ine §40. See also §1 and n. 14.

on Ld; written above by the scribe in E

Bessere Übs.: ‘Wenn jemand von einer Grafschaft fort in andere Grafschaft’; s. d. Gl 1b. 11—12. 18a. Q übertrug nur erste Hälfte des Wortes boldgetæl, die ‘Herrschaftsgut, manerium’ bedeuten kann [so in Engl. Ortsnamen; nddt. büttel ‘Dorf’; Jellinghaus in Anglia 20, 270]. Ich ziehe den Einfall im Wb, es liege hier eine Vorstufe des Hundred vor, ausdrücklich zurück. ‘Haus, Wohnung’ übs. Jacobs Namen der Gebäude (Diss. Kiel) 71 falsch

Better translation: ‘If anyone from one shire away into another shire’; see that word in Gl 1b. 11—12. 18a. Q rendered only the first half of the word boldgetæl, which can mean ‘lordship estate, manerium’ [so in English place-names; Low German büttel ‘village’; Jellinghaus in Anglia 20, 270]. I expressly withdraw the suggestion in the Wb that we have here a precursor of the hundred. Jacobs Namen der Gebäude (Diss. Kiel) 71 wrongly translates ‘house, dwelling’
Lies ‘Ealdorman, in dessen Grafschaft er bisher Vassall gewesen ist’; vgl. Wb: Relativum D
Read ‘ealdorman in whose shire he has hitherto been a vassal’; cf. Wb: Relativum D
V As 1, 1 erfordert Zeugnis (‘behördliche Aufsicht’ wie o. 34⁸) des Gerichts zur Herrensuche; s. d. Gl 3. 7
V As 1, 1 requires the witness (‘official supervision’, as above 34⁸) of the court for seeking a lord; see that word in Gl 3. 7

Vgl. Gl Gefolge 8c. 26; Freizügigkeit 1. Gegenüber Ine 39 büsst bei Af nicht der abziehende Mann, sondern der aufnehmende Herr, empfängt diese Busse und gibt den Urlaub nicht der frühere Herr, sondern der Staat, und ist das Strafgeld vervielfacht: die Vassallität ist in zwei Jahrhunderten von einer mehr privaten zur politischen Einrichtung geworden. Q stellt sich alles Abwandern Abhängiger gemäss dem Zustande in Normannenzeit vor als Übertritt von einem Herrschaftsgut ins andere

Cf. Gl Gefolge 8c. 26; Freizügigkeit 1. As against Ine 39, in Af it is not the departing man who pays compensation but the lord who receives him; it is not the former lord but the state that receives this compensation and grants leave; and the fine is multiplied: in two centuries vassalage has changed from a more private into a political institution. Q imagines all departure of dependants, in accordance with conditions in the Norman period, as a transfer from one lordship estate to another

Lit. ‘collection of habitations.’ Liebermann (iii. 58) understands boldgetæl to mean ‘county.’ In Alfred’s time each county had an ealdorman of its own. The word ealdorman (like scir) is sometimes used in a more general sense, but it is rather difficult to believe that Alfred would use the word in his laws, otherwise than in its technical meaning.

note.label: district
note.seg: boldgetale, literally “a number of houses”. Bishop Wasrferth uses it several times to translate provincia.
